text:
leo: hey team, Leo here - first week on runtime. trying to follow the "build from source" steps on my dev laptop (Win11 + WSL2 Ubuntu 22.04). enabled WSL GPU support and installed CUDA toolkit, but bazel link fails. who should I bug for a quick setup sanity check?

rachel: welcome! we've seen a bunch of WSL quirks. paste the exact error and the output of `ls /dev | grep nvidia` + `nvidia-smi` in WSL.

leo: error pasted below
```
ERROR: /home/leo/code/runtime/BUILD:58:1: Linking of rule '//runtime:serve' failed (Exit 1): gcc failed: error executing command ...
/usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lcudart
/usr/bin/ld: undefined reference to `__cudaRegisterFatBinary'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
INFO: Build completed, 1 target failed.
```
and in WSL:
```
$ nvidia-smi
NVIDIA-SMI has failed because it couldn't communicate with the NVIDIA driver. Make sure that the latest NVIDIA driver is installed and running.

$ ls /dev | grep nvidia || true

# nothing
```

jake: yeah that lines up - WSL needs the Windows NVIDIA driver + WSL CUDA support. Did you install the WSL-specific driver on the Windows host? Run from Windows: `nvidia-smi` and check driver version. In WSL you should see /dev/nvidia* devices. If those are missing, the linker can't find libcuda/cudart at runtime/link.

leo: on Windows `nvidia-smi` shows Driver Version: 531.79 and CUDA Version: 12.2. I followed MS docs and installed NVIDIA Studio driver with CUDA WSL support. rebooted. still nothing in WSL.

irene: two things to check: 1) Are you using Hyper-V vs WSLg? (should be WSL2). 2) Did you enable the WSL feature that exposes GPU? `wsl --update` then `wsl --shutdown` then restart WSL. Also ensure the distro is on WSL2 (`wsl -l -v`). Third, check Windows Feature "Virtual Machine Platform" enabled.

leo: distro is 2. I ran `wsl --update` and `wsl --shutdown`. still empty /dev.

rachel: if WSL still doesn't expose devices, easier path for now: use our remote dev workstation or the dev container on a Linux VM. We have a pre-provisioned DevBox with CUDA that you can SSH into. Ping infra for access or request a devbox via IT. For local dev, some folks dual-boot or use a native Ubuntu VM with PCI passthrough. WSL GPU support is still flaky on some machines.

jake: another workaround: build with `--define=use_cuda=false` for a host-only build if you just want to iterate on non-GPU changes, then run integration tests on CI/devbox. Also set `BAZEL_LINKOPTS="-L/usr/local/cuda/lib64"` if you have the toolkit in WSL and the lib exists. But again, without /dev/nvidia devices you won't get runtime GPU.

leo: thanks - I don't want to block others. I'll switch to remote devbox for full GPU builds. can someone point me to the devbox request flow?

devx-bot: DevX tip: For new runtime devs, request a GPU devbox by filing a ticket at https://redwood.internal/it/devbox with subject "Runtime GPU devbox - <your name>". Include machine preference (A100/T4) and estimated duration. If you need immediate access, ping @infra on Slack. Using the dev container image `gcr.io/redwood-runtime/dev:cuda-12.2-2025-03` on the devbox gives a reproducible build environment.

irene: also add this to your onboarding checklist: set `CUDA_HOME` in your `~/.bazelrc` or export in your shell and run `bazel clean --expunge` after switching envs. For WSL users, we recommend using remote devbox for now.

leo: great, filing ticket now. thanks for the quick triage and tips. I'll update the thread once I'm on the devbox. :rocket:
